definitions.explanation: A layer of fabric placed between the outer fabric and lining of a garment to add stiffness, shape, and structure. Used in collars, cuffs, waistbands, and other parts that need to hold their form.

notes:
A tailoring and sewing term composed of ⟦{芯|しん}→芯：03888_shin⟧ (core) and {地|じ} (cloth, fabric). Interlining is essential in garment construction, especially for structured clothing like suits, jackets, and dress shirts. There are two main types: {接着芯|せっちゃくしん} (fusible/iron-on interfacing) and {縫|ぬ}い{付|つ}け⟦{芯|しん}→芯：03888_shin⟧ (sew-in interfacing).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {接着|せっちゃく}{芯地|しんじ}: fusible interlining (iron-on type)
- {芯地|しんじ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{貼|は}る→貼る：10447_haru⟧: to apply interlining
- {芯地|しんじ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{入|い}れる→入れる：01098_ireru⟧: to insert interlining
- ⟦{不織布|ふしょくふ}→不織布：28792_fushokufu⟧{芯地|しんじ}: non-woven interlining

RELATED WORDS:
- {接着芯|せっちゃくしん}: fusible interfacing — commonly shortened from {接着|せっちゃく}{芯地|しんじ}
- ⟦{裏地|うらじ}→裏地：07101_uraji⟧: lining — the fabric on the inside of a garment, distinct from interlining
